edition_identity.status: Latest official edition according to Chaosium's current rules catalog.
edition_identity.signature_setting: 1920s classic era, with official support for many other periods.
edition_identity.baseline: Classic Call of Cthulhu rather than Pulp Cthulhu.

five_minute_explanation: One participant is the Keeper of Arcane Lore, who presents the mystery, world, non-player characters, clues, and threats.
Each other participant controls an investigator and describes what that person says and attempts.
The usual rhythm is description, questions, declared action, automatic resolution or a percentile roll, consequence, and a new choice.
Most tests succeed when 1D100 is equal to or below a skill or characteristic; lower rolls can achieve stronger levels of success.
Investigation, judgment, and survival matter more than winning fights; discovering the truth may itself carry a cost.
recommended_learning_order: Alone Against the Flames or another official solo tutorial

steps.name: Keeper frames the situation
steps.description: The Keeper describes what the investigators can perceive and what is happening now.

steps.name: Players ask questions and declare actions
steps.description: Players describe intentions in ordinary language, such as interviewing a witness, searching a desk, checking an archive, following a suspect, or leaving before the thing in the cellar reaches them.

steps.name: Keeper decides whether a roll is needed
steps.description: No roll is required for routine actions without meaningful uncertainty or consequence. A roll is used when the outcome is uncertain and dramatically important.

steps.name: Agree on the goal and stakes
steps.description: The player and Keeper should understand what success accomplishes and what failure may change.

steps.name: Resolve the action
steps.description: Roll percentile dice against a skill, characteristic, Luck, Sanity, or an opposed value.

steps.name: Narrate the result
steps.description: The Keeper applies the result to the fiction. Failure should usually introduce cost, delay, danger, incomplete information, suspicion, or a changed situation rather than simply stopping play.

steps.name: Follow the new lead
steps.description: The group updates notes, chooses a new avenue of inquiry, reacts to consequences, and repeats the loop.

investigation_pattern: Receive or discover a troubling situation.
Gather testimony, documents, physical evidence, and historical context.
Follow leads to new people or locations.
Discover the human conspiracy, Mythos influence, or both.
Choose whether to expose, interrupt, contain, escape, or confront the threat.
Face the aftermath and determine what the investigators learned or lost.

session_zero_and_table_practice.purpose: Agree on expectations before horror content begins.
discuss: The intended era, tone, and approximate campaign length.
Whether the game is bleak, pulpy, comedic in small doses, or strictly serious.
Topics that should not appear at all.
Topics that may occur off-screen but should not be described.
How players can pause, rewind, fade out, or leave a scene without having to justify discomfort.
How temporary or indefinite insanity will be portrayed respectfully.
How much character death, betrayal, helplessness, and loss the group wants.
Whether investigators are expected to remain cooperative.
How absences and replacement investigators will be handled.
session_zero_and_table_practice.best_practice_note: These table-safety procedures are recommended play practices, not percentile mechanics.

notation.D100: A result from 1 to 100, usually read using two ten-sided dice.

dice_and_notation.general_rule: Lower is usually better. To succeed, roll equal to or below the relevant target value.

other_dice_notation.meaning: Roll two six-sided dice and add them.
Roll one six-sided die and add 2.
Use a three-result method, commonly half of a D6 rounded up.

regular_success.requirement: Roll equal to or below the full skill or characteristic.
regular_success.example: Spot Hidden 60 succeeds on 60 or lower.

hard_success.requirement: Roll equal to or below one-half of the skill or characteristic, rounded down.

extreme_success.requirement: Roll equal to or below one-fifth of the skill or characteristic, rounded down.

critical_success.note: The Keeper gives an especially favorable result appropriate to the declared goal.

failure.requirement: Roll above the relevant target number.

fumble.requirement: A roll of 100, or 96–100 when the tested value is below 50.
fumble.note: A fumble creates a particularly bad result appropriate to the situation.

difficulty_guidance.use_when: A trained person has a reasonable chance and conditions are not unusually hostile.
The action is difficult, opposed by a capable obstacle, rushed, or performed under serious disadvantage.
The action approaches the practical limits of human capability.

success_levels.important_keeper_principle: Call for a roll only when failure would matter. Do not ask for repeated rolls until someone eventually succeeds unless the situation meaningfully changes.

bonus_and_penalty_dice.purpose: Represent favorable or unfavorable circumstances without changing the investigator's printed skill.

procedure: Roll one units die and two tens dice.
Combine the units die with each tens die.
Use the lower result.
Roll one units die and two tens dice.
Combine the units die with each tens die.
Use the higher result.

bonus_and_penalty_dice.cancellation: One bonus die and one penalty die cancel each other.
typical_uses: Strong leverage in a social encounter

opposed_rolls.when_used: Use when two active sides are directly competing and both results matter.
procedure: Each side rolls the appropriate skill or characteristic.
Compare levels of success.
Critical beats Extreme; Extreme beats Hard; Hard beats Regular; Regular beats Failure; Failure beats Fumble.
On the same level of success, the side with the higher relevant skill or characteristic wins.
If the relevant values are also equal, the lower D100 result wins.
examples: Stealth versus an observer's ability to detect the investigator.
Strength versus Strength when two people struggle over an object.
Charm, Fast Talk, Intimidate, or Persuade against a resisting character when the Keeper decides an opposed roll is warranted.

pushed_rolls.definition: A player may sometimes make one final attempt after a failed skill or characteristic roll.
requirements: The player explains what the investigator does differently or why the renewed attempt is more forceful, time-consuming, risky, or desperate.
The Keeper decides whether the new approach justifies a pushed roll.
The Keeper should make the heightened risk clear before the dice are rolled.

outcomes.success: The investigator achieves the revised goal.
outcomes.failure: The Keeper applies a serious consequence connected to the announced stakes.

cannot_normally_push: A roll that the Keeper determines cannot logically be attempted again
examples_of_different_approaches: Taking longer and dismantling a lock instead of trying the same pick again.
Threatening to reveal evidence after a failed polite interview.
Using a crowbar after failing to force a door by hand.
Continuing to study a disturbing text through exhaustion, risking discovery or mental harm.

luck.starting_value: For the official beginner creation method, roll 3D6 and multiply the total by 5.

luck_roll.use: Tests external chance rather than trained ability.
luck_roll.success: Roll equal to or below current Luck.
luck_roll.group_luck: When the Keeper calls for a group Luck roll, the investigator with the lowest Luck among those affected makes the roll.

examples: Whether a nearby abandoned vehicle still has fuel.
Whether a useful object happens to be within reach.
Whether a late-night cab appears in time.

optional_spending.status: Full-rule option that should be confirmed by the Keeper before play.
optional_spending.basic_concept: A player may spend current Luck to lower certain failed roll results by the same number of points, permanently reducing current Luck until it later improves.
optional_spending.limits: The complete rulebook defines rolls and situations on which Luck may not be spent. Do not assume every roll can be altered.

decision_rule: Use a skill when trained action can influence the result.
Use a characteristic when innate capacity is the direct issue and no skill fits.
Use Luck when the question is external chance or coincidence.
Use a group Luck roll only when the circumstance affects the group together.
luck.spending_luck_scope: Luck spending is a complete-rule option. Confirm its availability and prohibited uses with the Keeper Rulebook and the table before play.

investigation.core_principle: A sensible approach should reveal the core information needed to continue; rolls are best used for speed, depth, interpretation, stealth, danger, or additional leverage.

clue_types.core_clue: Required to understand or reach the next major part of the scenario; should have robust access.
clue_types.supporting_clue: Confirms, contextualizes, or narrows a theory.
clue_types.directional_clue: Points to a person, place, object, date, or record.
clue_types.warning_clue: Signals danger, cost, timing, or a false assumption.
clue_types.solution_clue: Reveals how a ritual, creature, device, or human plan may be interrupted or contained.
clue_types.character_clue: Reveals motive, relationship, guilt, fear, or personal stakes.

player_method: revisit old evidence after new discoveries
keeper_failure_results: the clue is found but costs time
anti_bottleneck_rules: never hide all routes behind the same skill
do not make repeated identical rolls
offer recaps of facts investigators would remember
let expertise matter without replacing player decisions

procedure: state the desired outcome
identify the NPC's motive and limits
choose Charm, Fast Talk, Intimidate, Persuade, evidence, status, or another approach
roleplay or summarize
roll only if uncertain and consequential
apply an outcome within what the NPC could plausibly agree to

skill_distinctions.fast_talk: Rapid deception or misdirection, usually with short-lived effect.
skill_distinctions.intimidate: Threats, pressure, or displays of force.
skill_distinctions.persuade: Reasoned argument that normally takes more time.
skill_distinctions.psychology: Reading motives and behavior; it does not compel someone.

limits: A social success is not mind control.
A lie may secure short-term action without permanently changing belief.
Intimidation can create later hostility or reporting.
Credit Rating can open social doors but cannot erase evidence, law, or immediate danger.
Psychology reads behavior; it does not reveal objective truth.

sanity.purpose: SAN measures an investigator's resilience when confronted with horror and impossible truths. It is a horror-fiction game mechanic, not a clinical model of real-world mental health.

procedure: Roll 1D100 against current SAN.
If the roll is equal to or below current SAN, apply the smaller loss listed before the slash.
If the roll is above current SAN, apply the larger loss listed after the slash.

sanity.involuntary_reaction: Any SAN loss can justify a brief involuntary reaction narrated by the Keeper, appropriate to the scene.

temporary_insanity.trigger: Lose 5 or more SAN from one Sanity roll, then succeed on an INT roll.
effects: A bout of madness may occur.
The Keeper may add or alter a backstory entry.
A phobia or mania may be added.
Delusions may occur during the temporary-insanity period.
A player may request a reality check using a Sanity roll.
temporary_insanity.counterintuitive_note: On this INT roll, success means the investigator fully comprehends the horror and becomes temporarily insane; failure means the mind suppresses or fails to integrate it.

indefinite_insanity.trigger: Lose one-fifth or more of the investigator's starting SAN during one in-game day.
indefinite_insanity.effect: The investigator remains vulnerable to bouts of madness and related effects until recovery under the full rules.
indefinite_insanity.recovery_note: Long-term care and recovery are campaign matters described more fully in the Keeper Rulebook.

sanity.maximum_sanity: Maximum SAN is reduced by Cthulhu Mythos skill: 99 minus Cthulhu Mythos.
table_care: Agree on how loss of control will be narrated.
Do not use the mechanic to mock real diagnoses or players' lived experiences.
The player should remain involved in portraying the investigator whenever practical.
Fade out or revise a result that crosses an agreed boundary.
keeper_preparation: assign loss notation before the scene
decide whether repeat exposure changes the roll
keep the player involved whenever practical
distinguish frightening imagery from loss of agency
portrayal_guardrails: Treat SAN as a horror-fiction resilience mechanic, not a diagnosis.
Do not imitate a player's real condition for entertainment.
Use concrete sensory or behavioral effects rather than stigmatizing labels.
Permit pause, fade, or replacement of a result that crosses a boundary.

combat.core_warning: Combat is dangerous. Mythos entities may be stronger than humans, resistant to weapons, or impossible to defeat by ordinary force.

round_structure.initiative: Act from highest DEX to lowest DEX.
round_structure.round_length: Long enough for each participant to take one significant action.
typical_actions: Administer emergency aid when fictionally possible
Take another significant action approved by the Keeper

dodge.tie_rule: A tied level of success favors the defender; the attacker must achieve a better level.

fight_back.tie_rule: A tied level of success favors the initiating attacker; the defender must achieve a better level to counterattack.

close_combat.result: The winner avoids harm; a successful attacker or successful fight-back defender deals damage as appropriate.

firearms.readied_weapon: A readied firearm acts at DEX +50 for turn order.
firearms.multiple_handgun_shots: Firing two or three handgun shots in one round gives one penalty die to each shot.
firearms.point_blank: Within one-fifth of the shooter's DEX in feet, the shooter gains one bonus die.
firearms.defense: A target cannot literally dodge a bullet but may dive for cover. A successful Dodge imposes one penalty die on the attack and costs the target's next attack.

extreme_damage.blunt: Maximum weapon damage plus maximum Damage Bonus, when applicable.
extreme_damage.impaling: Maximum weapon damage plus an additional weapon-damage roll and any applicable Damage Bonus.
extreme_damage.fight_back_limit: A fight-back result normally deals regular damage even if its roll is Extreme.

fighting_maneuvers.purpose: Disarm, knock down, seize, restrain, shove, or achieve another non-damage goal.
procedure: Resolve as a Fighting attack.
The defender may Dodge or fight back.
Compare Build.
The attacker takes one penalty die per point of Build disadvantage, to a maximum of two.
A maneuver is ineffective when the target exceeds the attacker's Build by three or more.

combat.outnumbered: After a character has dodged or fought back once in a round, later melee attacks against that character receive one bonus die. Firearms are excluded.
combat_start_checklist: identify surprise or readied weapons through the fiction
order by DEX, applying readied-firearm timing
note cover, exits, light, hazards, and civilians
turn_decision_tree: Can the investigator leave or reach safety?
Is the weapon ready and in range?
Will an action expose the investigator to later attacks?
Is Dodge, fight back, or diving for cover available when attacked?
What happens if the adversary survives this round?

close_combat_tie_matrix.attack_vs_dodge_same_level: defender succeeds; attacker must achieve a better level
close_combat_tie_matrix.attack_vs_fight_back_same_level: initiating attacker succeeds; defender must achieve a better level
close_combat_tie_matrix.fight_back_success: defender avoids harm and deals regular damage
close_combat_tie_matrix.dodge_success: defender avoids harm and deals no damage

firearm_notes: readied firearms alter turn-order DEX by +50
two or three handgun shots impose one penalty die on each shot
point-blank range grants a bonus die under the stated formula
diving for cover imposes a penalty die if Dodge succeeds and costs the target's next attack
use exact weapon entries for ranges, ammunition, malfunctions, bursts, and automatic fire
morale_framework: ordinary people may flee after a major wound
cultists may retreat to protect a ritual or leader
professionals seek cover and favorable position
creatures follow their described instincts rather than universal tactics

damage_wounds_healing.taking_damage: Subtract damage from current HP; HP does not go below zero.

major_wound.trigger: A single attack deals damage equal to or greater than half maximum HP.
major_wound.immediate_effect: Make a CON roll or fall unconscious.

zero_hit_points.without_major_wound: The investigator is unconscious but is not dying from that injury sequence.
zero_hit_points.with_major_wound: The investigator is dying and must make repeated CON rolls under the full procedure until stabilized or dead.

damage_wounds_healing.instant_death: A single attack that deals damage equal to or greater than maximum HP may kill instantly.

first_aid.time_window: Normally within one hour of the injury.
first_aid.effect: Restore 1 HP and potentially rouse an unconscious character.
first_aid.dying_use: Temporarily stabilizes a dying character so Medicine can be attempted.

medicine.time: At least one hour with suitable supplies.
medicine.dying_use: Follows successful First Aid and supports longer-term survival under the full rules.

natural_healing.major_wound: Make a weekly CON healing roll; success restores 1D3 HP and an Extreme success restores 2D3 HP.
natural_healing.major_wound_removed: Removed when an Extreme healing success occurs or current HP reaches at least half maximum HP.

transitions: major wound if one attack is at least half maximum HP
unconscious if a major-wound CON roll fails
zero HP state if damage reduces HP to zero

zero_without_major_wound.result: unconscious, not dying under this procedure

zero_with_major_wound.result: dying; requires stabilization and repeated checks under the full procedure

instant_death.condition: one attack deals at least maximum HP

environmental_hazard_design: choose damage scale by likely lethality
for ongoing exposure, define the roll and damage interval
for drowning or asphyxiation, track failed CON and subsequent damage
for poison, define onset, damage, and whether an Extreme CON result mitigates it

magic.tone: Mythos magic is dangerous knowledge that manipulates forces human beings do not safely understand.

magic_points.when_zero: Further magic-point costs are normally taken from HP one-for-one.

first_casting.normal_requirement: A newly learned spell normally requires a Hard POW roll the first time it is cast.
first_casting.pushed_casting: A second attempt may be made by paying the cost again. On a failed pushed casting roll, the spell still operates but dire consequences affect the caster.

magic.after_first_success: Later castings of that spell normally do not require the initial casting roll, although the spell's listed costs and procedures still apply.
player_guidance: Do not assume learning a spell is automatically beneficial.
Read, translate, test, and cast Mythos material only after considering time, SAN, magic-point, and narrative costs.
The Keeper Rulebook and scenarios contain the actual spell descriptions.
casting_sequence: confirm the investigator has learned the spell
read the exact official spell entry
if never successfully cast, make the first-casting Hard POW roll
on ordinary failure, decide whether to stop or push
if pushed, pay the costs again
resolve success or the spell plus dire consequence on pushed failure
record that later castings normally skip the first-casting roll
safety_and_tone: Magic is evidence of dangerous reality, not a balanced player power list.
Spells may impose SAN, HP, MP, time, material, social, or narrative costs.
The Keeper should not reveal hidden spell consequences before the fiction supports that knowledge.

chases.scope: The complete chase subsystem is in the Keeper Rulebook and is not reproduced here.
beginner_fallback: frame one obstacle at a time
use a relevant vehicle, movement, navigation, or characteristic roll
let success improve position and failure add cost or reduce options
end when capture, escape, or a decisive location is reached
do_not_do: do not roll the same check repeatedly without changing stakes
do not decide the winner from one roll when the scene is intended to be a major set piece

skill_checks.no_improvement: If the result is equal to or below the current skill, the skill does not increase.
skill_checks.cleanup: Erase the check after resolving the improvement roll.

players.mistake: Treating the game like a tactical monster-fighting campaign.
players.correction: Investigate first. Ordinary weapons may not solve a Mythos threat.
Describe where and how the investigator searches and what they hope to find.

players.mistake: Hiding every clue from the other players.
players.correction: Share case information unless secrecy creates agreed, productive drama.

players.mistake: Assuming a failed roll means nothing happens.
players.correction: Failure often means cost, delay, danger, or incomplete understanding.

players.mistake: Pushing a roll without changing the approach.
players.correction: Explain the new method and accept the announced consequence.

players.mistake: Using Occult and Cthulhu Mythos as synonyms.
players.correction: Occult covers human traditions and esoteric beliefs; Cthulhu Mythos represents dangerous knowledge of inhuman reality.

players.mistake: Building an investigator with no reason to join the case.
players.correction: Create a personal, professional, or relational hook before play.
Escaping with knowledge may be the correct victory.

keepers.mistake: Hiding a vital clue behind one roll.
keepers.correction: Give the core clue when the investigators use a sensible approach; use the roll for speed, detail, danger, or interpretation.

keepers.mistake: Calling for rolls for routine actions.
keepers.correction: Roll only when uncertainty and consequences matter.

keepers.mistake: Requiring the exact solution imagined by the scenario.
keepers.correction: Judge reasonable player plans by their fictional logic.

keepers.mistake: Using Sanity loss as comedy at a player's expense.
keepers.correction: Use the mechanic to support horror and character change within agreed boundaries.

keepers.mistake: Revealing the monster too clearly and too early.
keepers.correction: Let evidence, effects, witnesses, and partial perception build dread.

keepers.mistake: Punishing caution until players rush blindly.
keepers.correction: Allow preparation to matter while maintaining an active threat timeline.

keepers.mistake: Running every NPC as either completely helpful or completely obstructive.
keepers.correction: Give NPCs motives, fears, partial knowledge, and conditions for cooperation.
Advance the scenario timeline when investigators delay, attract attention, or reveal themselves.

additional.correction: Use it to read behavior and motives; evidence still establishes facts.

additional.mistake: Calling for Spot Hidden without a described search.
additional.correction: Clarify where, how, and what the investigator is trying to notice.

additional.mistake: Making every failed social roll end the conversation.
additional.correction: Change attitude, price, conditions, timing, or consequences instead.

additional.mistake: Forgetting starting SAN when tracking indefinite insanity.
additional.correction: Record both starting and current SAN and tally losses by in-game day.

additional.mistake: Letting successful preparation have no benefit.
additional.correction: Use automatic success, bonus dice, lower difficulty, better positioning, or reduced consequences when justified.

additional.mistake: Giving full statistics to every NPC before defining motives.
additional.correction: Prepare goal, fear, knowledge, leverage, and behavior first.

additional.mistake: Using a monster as a bag of HP.
additional.correction: Run its instincts, movement, defenses, powers, and objective as described by the source.

additional.mistake: Awarding improvement checks for trivial practice rolls.
additional.correction: Require successful use in meaningful play.

worked_examples.setup: Library Use 55; ordinary archive search; roll 42.
worked_examples.resolution: 42 is at or below 55, so the roll is a Regular success.
worked_examples.teaching_point: A successful meaningful skill use may be checked once for later improvement.

worked_examples.setup: Spot Hidden 60; concealed detail requires Hard success; roll 28.
worked_examples.resolution: Half of 60 is 30. A 28 is a Hard success.
worked_examples.teaching_point: The Keeper sets the required level before the roll when possible.

worked_examples.setup: Locksmith 65; a near-impossible mechanism requires Extreme success; roll 12.
worked_examples.resolution: One-fifth of 65 is 13. A 12 is an Extreme success.
worked_examples.teaching_point: Round half and fifth values down.

worked_examples.setup: Any suitable skill roll produces 01.
worked_examples.resolution: The result is Critical.
worked_examples.teaching_point: The Keeper gives an especially favorable result connected to the declared goal, not an unrelated miracle.

worked_examples.setup: Locksmith 35; roll 97.
worked_examples.resolution: Because the skill is below 50, 96–100 is a fumble range; 97 fumbles.
worked_examples.teaching_point: Fumble range depends on the tested value.

worked_examples.setup: Library Use 70; roll 97.
worked_examples.resolution: This is a failure but not normally a fumble; only 100 fumbles when the tested value is 50 or more.
worked_examples.teaching_point: High skills reduce the fumble range.

worked_examples.setup: Units die 4; tens dice 20 and 60; one bonus die.
worked_examples.resolution: Possible results are 24 and 64; use 24.
worked_examples.teaching_point: Bonus and penalty dice replace only the tens digit.

worked_examples.setup: Units die 1; tens dice 20 and 40; one penalty die.
worked_examples.resolution: Possible results are 21 and 41; use 41.
worked_examples.teaching_point: A penalty die uses the worse result.

worked_examples.setup: One bonus die from excellent tools and one penalty die from darkness.
worked_examples.resolution: They cancel; roll ordinary percentile dice unless another modifier remains.
worked_examples.teaching_point: Do not roll both extra dice after cancellation.

worked_examples.setup: Stealth achieves Hard; opposing detection achieves Regular.
worked_examples.resolution: Hard beats Regular.
worked_examples.teaching_point: Compare success levels before comparing skill ratings.

worked_examples.setup: Both sides achieve Regular; skills are 65 and 50.
worked_examples.resolution: The side with 65 wins the tied level.
worked_examples.teaching_point: Only use the lower D100 tiebreak when relevant values are also equal.

worked_examples.setup: A failed Locksmith roll is retried by removing hinges with tools, risking noise.
worked_examples.resolution: On success, the revised method opens the cabinet.
worked_examples.teaching_point: A push changes the approach or stakes; it is not a free reroll.

worked_examples.setup: The pushed hinge-removal roll fails after the Keeper warns that someone may hear.
worked_examples.resolution: Apply the announced serious consequence and do not offer another push.
worked_examples.teaching_point: The consequence should arise from the method and situation.

worked_examples.setup: Current Luck 48; roll 44 to see whether keys are in a nearby car.
worked_examples.resolution: The Luck roll succeeds.
worked_examples.teaching_point: Use Luck for external chance, not as a replacement for a more appropriate skill.

worked_examples.setup: Present investigators have Luck 60, 52, and 35.
worked_examples.resolution: The investigator with Luck 35 makes the group Luck roll.
worked_examples.teaching_point: The least lucky present investigator represents the group.

worked_examples.setup: SAN 62; loss 0/1D6; roll 44.
worked_examples.resolution: The Sanity roll succeeds and the investigator loses 0 SAN.
worked_examples.teaching_point: Use the amount before the slash on success.

worked_examples.setup: SAN 62; loss 1/1D8; roll 77.
worked_examples.resolution: The roll fails; lose 1D8 SAN.
worked_examples.teaching_point: Use the amount after the slash on failure.

worked_examples.setup: A single Sanity roll causes 6 SAN loss; INT 70; follow-up roll 51.
worked_examples.resolution: The INT roll succeeds, so the investigator comprehends the horror and becomes temporarily insane for 1D10 hours.
worked_examples.teaching_point: The INT test is intentionally counterintuitive: success triggers temporary insanity.

worked_examples.setup: A single roll causes 5 SAN loss; INT 60; follow-up roll 84.
worked_examples.resolution: The INT roll fails, so temporary insanity is avoided at that moment.
worked_examples.teaching_point: The mind fails to integrate the experience.

worked_examples.setup: Starting SAN 60; the investigator loses 12 SAN during one in-game day.
worked_examples.resolution: Twelve is one-fifth of 60, so the indefinite-insanity threshold is reached.
worked_examples.teaching_point: Track loss against starting SAN within the in-game day, not current SAN.

worked_examples.setup: Attacker and dodging defender both obtain Hard success.
worked_examples.resolution: The defender avoids the attack because the attacker must beat Dodge.
worked_examples.teaching_point: Ties favor Dodge.

worked_examples.setup: Attacker and fight-back defender both obtain Regular success.
worked_examples.resolution: The initiating attacker wins because fight back must beat the attacker's level.
worked_examples.teaching_point: Ties favor the initiating attacker against fight back.

worked_examples.setup: Attacker gets Regular; defender fighting back gets Hard.
worked_examples.resolution: The defender avoids the attack and deals regular damage to the attacker.
worked_examples.teaching_point: Fight back is both defense and counterattack.

worked_examples.setup: A club deals 1D6 plus 1D4 Damage Bonus; the initiating attack is Extreme.
worked_examples.resolution: Deal maximum weapon damage plus maximum Damage Bonus: 6 + 4 = 10.
worked_examples.teaching_point: Blunt extreme damage maximizes the listed components.

worked_examples.setup: A handgun deals 1D10 and the attack is Extreme.
worked_examples.resolution: Deal maximum weapon damage plus another weapon-damage roll, following the impaling rule.
worked_examples.teaching_point: Impaling extreme damage differs from blunt extreme damage.

worked_examples.setup: Maximum HP 12; one attack deals 6 damage.
worked_examples.resolution: Six is at least half maximum HP, so mark a major wound and make a CON roll to remain conscious.
worked_examples.teaching_point: The threshold applies to one attack, not accumulated damage.

worked_examples.setup: An investigator reaches 0 HP through several smaller injuries and has no major wound.
worked_examples.resolution: The investigator falls unconscious but is not dying from this procedure.
worked_examples.teaching_point: Zero HP alone is not always the dying condition.

worked_examples.setup: An investigator with a major wound reaches 0 HP.
worked_examples.resolution: The investigator is dying and requires stabilization under the full procedure.
worked_examples.teaching_point: Major wound plus zero HP creates the lethal state.

worked_examples.setup: Maximum HP 11; one attack deals 11 or more damage.
worked_examples.resolution: The single blow can cause instant death under the rule.
worked_examples.teaching_point: This compares one attack's damage with maximum HP.

worked_examples.setup: A wounded investigator receives successful First Aid within the allowed window.
worked_examples.resolution: Restore 1 HP; it may also rouse an unconscious character or stabilize a dying one as applicable.
worked_examples.teaching_point: First Aid is immediate treatment, not full medical recovery.

worked_examples.setup: A physician has at least an hour and suitable supplies; Medicine succeeds.
worked_examples.resolution: Restore 1D3 HP under the standard summary.
worked_examples.teaching_point: Medicine requires more time and equipment than First Aid.

worked_examples.setup: Spot Hidden 45 is checked; improvement roll is 72.
worked_examples.resolution: Because 72 is above 45, add 1D10 to Spot Hidden and erase the check.
worked_examples.teaching_point: Improvement becomes less likely as a skill rises.

worked_examples.setup: Library Use 70 is checked; improvement roll is 43.
worked_examples.resolution: No increase occurs because the roll is not above the current skill; erase the check.
worked_examples.teaching_point: A successful use does not guarantee an increase.

worked_examples.setup: A newly learned spell is attempted for the first time; Hard POW roll succeeds.
worked_examples.resolution: Pay the listed costs and resolve the spell description.
worked_examples.teaching_point: The first-casting roll is separate from the spell's costs and effects.

worked_examples.setup: The first casting failed; the caster pays costs again and fails the pushed Hard POW roll.
worked_examples.resolution: The spell operates, but dire consequences affect the caster.
worked_examples.teaching_point: Pushed first casting gauges the harm of forcing the spell.

worked_examples.setup: Attacker Build 0 attempts to shove target Build 2.
worked_examples.resolution: The attacker takes two penalty dice on the Fighting maneuver.
worked_examples.teaching_point: Apply one penalty die per point of Build disadvantage, to the stated maximum.

worked_examples.setup: Attacker Build 0 attempts to wrestle target Build 3.
worked_examples.resolution: The maneuver is ineffective because the target exceeds the attacker's Build by three.
worked_examples.teaching_point: Some scale differences cannot be solved by a lucky maneuver roll.

worked_examples.setup: A defender has already dodged once this round and faces a second melee attacker.
worked_examples.resolution: The later melee attacker receives one bonus die.
worked_examples.teaching_point: Outnumbered applies after the first dodge or fight-back response in the round.

worked_examples.setup: DEX 55 and a firearm is ready at combat start.
worked_examples.resolution: Use DEX 105 for the firearm's turn-order placement.
worked_examples.teaching_point: The modifier affects order, not the Firearms skill value.

worked_examples.setup: A target successfully dives for cover against a firearm attack.
worked_examples.resolution: The shooter takes one penalty die and the target forfeits the next attack as specified.
worked_examples.teaching_point: This is not ordinary bullet dodging.

quick_reference.roll_under: Roll equal to or below the target.
success_levels: Fumble: 100, or 96–100 when the tested value is below 50
quick_reference.pushing: One justified final attempt with a serious announced consequence; not for combat or Sanity rolls.
quick_reference.bonus_die: Roll an extra tens die and use the lower result.
quick_reference.penalty_die: Roll an extra tens die and use the higher result.
quick_reference.sanity: Roll under current SAN; apply the loss before or after the slash.
quick_reference.temporary_insanity: Single SAN loss of 5+ followed by a successful INT roll.
quick_reference.major_wound: One attack deals at least half maximum HP.
quick_reference.zero_hp: Without a major wound: unconscious. With a major wound: dying.
quick_reference.combat_order: Highest DEX first; readied firearm uses DEX +50.
quick_reference.skill_improvement: For a checked skill, roll above the current value to gain 1D10.

missing_person.premise: A disappearance reveals hidden relationships, locations, and escalating danger.
missing_person.keeper_design_focus: Decide whether the missing person is victim, participant, transformed witness, or bait.

forbidden_text.name: Forbidden Text
forbidden_text.premise: A document, recording, translation, or archive connects ordinary scholarship to Mythos danger.
forbidden_text.keeper_design_focus: Treat access, translation, interpretation, and safe custody as separate problems.

cult_institution.name: Cult Inside an Institution
cult_institution.premise: A respected organization conceals a faction, ritual, or compromised leadership.
cult_institution.keeper_design_focus: Give innocent members, conflicted insiders, and institutional consequences.

isolated_community.name: Isolated Community
isolated_community.premise: A town, ship, expedition, island, or facility has shared secrets and limited escape.
isolated_community.keeper_design_focus: Track who controls transport, communication, food, shelter, and public opinion.

scientific_anomaly.name: Scientific Anomaly
scientific_anomaly.premise: Evidence violates accepted science and draws competing interpretations.
scientific_anomaly.keeper_design_focus: Provide repeatable observations but make comprehension costly or incomplete.

serial_pattern.name: Recurring Crime Pattern
serial_pattern.premise: Separate crimes reveal a ritual, timetable, geography, or nonhuman logic.
serial_pattern.keeper_design_focus: Build a pattern investigators can discover before the final occurrence.

inheritance.name: Inheritance and Family Secret
inheritance.premise: Property, letters, genealogy, or obligations pull investigators into an older pact.
inheritance.keeper_design_focus: Give family members different motives and partial truths.

expedition.name: Expedition Into the Unknown
expedition.premise: Travel and logistics frame discovery of a remote site or phenomenon.
expedition.keeper_design_focus: Make weather, supplies, guides, transport, and return routes meaningful without replacing investigation.

public_event.name: Public Event Goes Wrong
public_event.premise: A festival, lecture, performance, election, trial, or exhibition becomes the stage for Mythos activity.
public_event.keeper_design_focus: Use crowds, witnesses, publicity, and collateral consequences.

dream_infection.name: Dream or Memory Contagion
dream_infection.premise: Shared dreams, missing time, or altered memories point toward an external influence.
dream_infection.keeper_design_focus: Provide physical corroboration so the mystery is investigable.

artifact_chain.name: Artifact Changes Hands
artifact_chain.premise: An object moves through collectors, thieves, museums, estates, and cultists.
artifact_chain.keeper_design_focus: Every prior owner should reveal a new property, cost, or false belief.

closed_room.name: Impossible Crime
closed_room.premise: A crime appears physically impossible until hidden assumptions are challenged.
closed_room.keeper_design_focus: The solution may explain the method without making the underlying reality safe.

false_haunting.name: Human Crime Behind Apparent Haunting
false_haunting.premise: People exploit supernatural fear, while a separate real horror may or may not exist.
false_haunting.keeper_design_focus: Keep human and Mythos evidence distinguishable.

contaminated_site.name: Environmental Corruption
contaminated_site.premise: Water, soil, wildlife, architecture, or weather reveals a spreading influence.
contaminated_site.keeper_design_focus: Map progression and give investigators measurable signs.

academic_rivalry.name: Academic Rivalry
academic_rivalry.premise: Competing researchers race to publish, translate, excavate, or suppress evidence.
academic_rivalry.keeper_design_focus: Make reputation, access, and ethics as important as physical danger.

medical_mystery.name: Medical Mystery
medical_mystery.premise: Symptoms resist ordinary diagnosis and connect patients through place, object, ancestry, or exposure.
medical_mystery.keeper_design_focus: Respect real illness; distinguish fictional Mythos effects from real conditions.

law_enforcement_case.name: Official Investigation
law_enforcement_case.premise: Investigators have legal authority but face procedure, superiors, evidence rules, and public scrutiny.
law_enforcement_case.keeper_design_focus: Authority opens doors and creates accountability.

criminal_underworld.name: Underworld Inquiry
criminal_underworld.premise: Witnesses and evidence lie within illegal networks.
criminal_underworld.keeper_design_focus: Contacts demand payment, favors, protection, or proof of trust.

siege.name: Containment or Siege
siege.premise: A small group must survive or hold a location while learning what threatens it.
siege.keeper_design_focus: Information should create better choices, not merely explain inevitable attacks.

time_pressure_ritual.name: Ritual Countdown
time_pressure_ritual.premise: A ceremony or astronomical window creates a clear clock.
time_pressure_ritual.keeper_design_focus: Clues should reveal what each ritual component does and which interruptions matter.

identity_replacement.name: Identity and Replacement
identity_replacement.premise: A familiar person may be altered, duplicated, possessed, or impersonated.
identity_replacement.keeper_design_focus: Use behavioral, documentary, and physical evidence; avoid making Psychology a truth detector.

historical_echo.name: Past Event Repeats
historical_echo.premise: A current case mirrors an earlier disaster.
historical_echo.keeper_design_focus: Let investigators compare records, survivors, sites, and changed conditions.

patron_with_secret.name: Compromised Patron
patron_with_secret.premise: The person funding or directing the investigation hides a crucial motive.
patron_with_secret.keeper_design_focus: The patron's lie should complicate the case without invalidating every clue.

failed_occultism.name: Human Ritual Reaches Something Real
failed_occultism.premise: Ordinary occultists accidentally contact a genuine Mythos force.
failed_occultism.keeper_design_focus: Separate what the cultists believe from what actually answers.

one_sentence_summary.text: Players portray ordinary people investigating a frightening mystery, while the Keeper presents the world, clues, threats, and consequences; most uncertain actions are resolved by rolling percentile dice at or below a skill or characteristic.

what_kind_of_game_is_it.default_era: The signature setting is the 1920s, although official material supports modern-day and many other periods.
what_kind_of_game_is_it.central_premise: Investigators uncover clues that lead to deeper truths, dangerous people, unnatural forces, and sometimes entities that human beings are poorly equipped to understand or fight.
what_kind_of_game_is_it.important_expectation: This is not normally a combat-first or treasure-collection game. Learning what is happening, deciding whom to trust, preserving evidence, interrupting a ritual, escaping alive, or limiting a disaster may be a better victory than killing an enemy.

steps.name: Keeper frames the situation
steps.description: The Keeper describes what the investigators can perceive and what is happening now.

steps.name: Players ask questions and declare actions
steps.description: Players describe intentions in ordinary language, such as interviewing a witness, searching a desk, checking an archive, following a suspect, or leaving before the thing in the cellar reaches them.

steps.name: Keeper decides whether a roll is needed
steps.description: No roll is required for routine actions without meaningful uncertainty or consequence. A roll is used when the outcome is uncertain and dramatically important.

steps.name: Agree on the goal and stakes
steps.description: The player and Keeper should understand what success accomplishes and what failure may change.

steps.name: Resolve the action
steps.description: Roll percentile dice against a skill, characteristic, Luck, Sanity, or an opposed value.

steps.name: Narrate the result
steps.description: The Keeper applies the result to the fiction. Failure should usually introduce cost, delay, danger, incomplete information, suspicion, or a changed situation rather than simply stopping play.

steps.name: Follow the new lead
steps.description: The group updates notes, chooses a new avenue of inquiry, reacts to consequences, and repeats the loop.

procedure: Each side rolls the appropriate skill or characteristic.
Compare levels of success.
Critical beats Extreme; Extreme beats Hard; Hard beats Regular; Regular beats Failure; Failure beats Fumble.
On the same level of success, the side with the higher relevant skill or characteristic wins.
If the relevant values are also equal, the lower D100 result wins.
examples: Stealth versus an observer's ability to detect the investigator.
Strength versus Strength when two people struggle over an object.
Charm, Fast Talk, Intimidate, or Persuade against a resisting character when the Keeper decides an opposed roll is warranted.

pushed_rolls.definition: A player may sometimes make one final attempt after a failed skill or characteristic roll.
requirements: The player explains what the investigator does differently or why the renewed attempt is more forceful, time-consuming, risky, or desperate.
The Keeper decides whether the new approach justifies a pushed roll.
The Keeper should make the heightened risk clear before the dice are rolled.

outcomes.success: The investigator achieves the revised goal.
outcomes.failure: The Keeper applies a serious consequence connected to the announced stakes.

cannot_normally_push: A roll that the Keeper determines cannot logically be attempted again
examples_of_different_approaches: Taking longer and dismantling a lock instead of trying the same pick again.
Threatening to reveal evidence after a failed polite interview.
Using a crowbar after failing to force a door by hand.
Continuing to study a disturbing text through exhaustion, risking discovery or mental harm.

luck.starting_value: For the official beginner creation method, roll 3D6 and multiply the total by 5.

luck_roll.use: Tests external chance rather than trained ability.
luck_roll.success: Roll equal to or below current Luck.
luck_roll.group_luck: When the Keeper calls for a group Luck roll, the investigator with the lowest Luck among those affected makes the roll.

examples: Whether a nearby abandoned vehicle still has fuel.
Whether a useful object happens to be within reach.
Whether a late-night cab appears in time.

optional_spending.status: Full-rule option that should be confirmed by the Keeper before play.
optional_spending.basic_concept: A player may spend current Luck to lower certain failed roll results by the same number of points, permanently reducing current Luck until it later improves.
optional_spending.limits: The complete rulebook defines rolls and situations on which Luck may not be spent. Do not assume every roll can be altered.

creating_an_investigator.method: Official streamlined beginner method presented by the Chaosium Call of Cthulhu RPG Wiki.

steps.name: Choose a concept
instructions: Decide who the person was before the horror began.
Give the investigator a reason to become involved in the scenario.
Choose a concept that can cooperate with the other investigators.

steps.name: Assign characteristics

characteristics.POW: Power; will, spirit, and mental resilience.
characteristics.APP: Appearance; personal presence and physical appeal.
characteristics.INT: Intelligence; reasoning, intuition, and mental agility.

steps.procedure: Assign each number once among the eight characteristics.
steps.record: Write the full, half, and fifth values.

steps.name: Calculate secondary attributes
steps.instructions: Use the formulas in the derived_statistics section.

steps.name: Choose an occupation
instructions: Choose a profession appropriate to the scenario and era.
Select the occupation's eight relevant skills, or use a published occupation.
Credit Rating is also included in the occupation allocation.

steps.name: Assign occupation skill values
steps.instructions: Distribute these nine values among the eight occupation skills and Credit Rating.

steps.name: Choose personal-interest skills
steps.instructions: Choose four non-occupation skills and add 20 percentage points to each skill's printed base chance.

steps.name: Write a backstory
recommended_entries: A fear, vulnerability, obligation, or unresolved problem
steps.instruction: Two or three concise entries are enough to begin.

steps.name: Add final details
instructions: Name, pronouns, birthplace, residence, and age.
Ordinary gear expected for the occupation.
A reason to trust or know at least one other investigator.
Confirm the scenario hook with the Keeper.

cthulhu_mythos_skill.starting_rule: Normally begins at 0 and cannot receive ordinary creation points unless the Keeper explicitly approves an unusual concept.
cthulhu_mythos_skill.meaning: Represents dangerous understanding of the inhuman Mythos, not conventional occult knowledge.

creating_an_investigator.full_creation_note: The Keeper Rulebook and Investigator Handbook provide expanded occupations, point-allocation methods, age effects, finances, equipment, and other options.

hit_points.meaning: Physical endurance before unconsciousness, dying, or death rules apply.

magic_points.rounding: Characteristics in the streamlined method are multiples of 5.
magic_points.recovery: Spent magic points normally recover at 1 point per hour.

move.note: The full rules may adjust MOV for age and the relationship among STR, DEX, and SIZ.

damage_bonus_and_build.meaning: Damage Bonus adds to many close-combat attacks; Build compares physical scale for maneuvers.

principles: The skill name describes an area of competence, not a rigid button that solves every situation.
State the investigator's approach first; the Keeper selects the most appropriate skill.
A successful roll should achieve the agreed goal or provide useful progress.
Vital clues should not depend on a single fragile roll. Rolls can determine speed, extra detail, danger, or the quality of interpretation.
The Keeper may roll some perception or Psychology checks secretly when uncertainty itself improves the mystery.
A checked skill may be eligible to improve after the session or scenario.

social_skill_distinctions.fast_talk: Rapid deception or misdirection, usually with short-lived effect.
social_skill_distinctions.intimidate: Threats, pressure, or displays of force.
social_skill_distinctions.persuade: Reasoned argument that normally takes more time.
social_skill_distinctions.psychology: Reading motives and behavior; it does not compel someone.

habits_that_help: Write down every proper name and how it connects to the case.
Ask what is physically present rather than waiting for the Keeper to volunteer every detail.
Interview witnesses separately when their stories may conflict.
Check newspapers, property records, medical records, police files, archives, and local histories.
Revisit earlier clues after learning new facts.
Tell the Keeper your goal, not only the skill you want to roll.
Bring appropriate tools and establish an exit plan before entering a dangerous place.
Share clues with the group unless secrecy is a deliberate character choice accepted by the table.
Treat unexplained rituals, books, and artifacts as potentially dangerous evidence rather than ordinary treasure.
when_stuck: Review unresolved names, dates, symbols, addresses, and organizations.
Ask which lead has not been followed.
Return to a witness with new evidence.
Observe the suspect or location instead of immediately confronting it.
Ask the Keeper to recap facts the investigators would reasonably remember.
Use an Idea or Intelligence-based prompt only when the Keeper offers or permits it.

sanity_rules.purpose: SAN measures an investigator's resilience when confronted with horror and impossible truths. It is a horror-fiction game mechanic, not a clinical model of real-world mental health.

procedure: Roll 1D100 against current SAN.
If the roll is equal to or below current SAN, apply the smaller loss listed before the slash.
If the roll is above current SAN, apply the larger loss listed after the slash.

sanity_rules.involuntary_reaction: Any SAN loss can justify a brief involuntary reaction narrated by the Keeper, appropriate to the scene.

temporary_insanity.trigger: Lose 5 or more SAN from one Sanity roll, then succeed on an INT roll.
effects: A bout of madness may occur.
The Keeper may add or alter a backstory entry.
A phobia or mania may be added.
Delusions may occur during the temporary-insanity period.
A player may request a reality check using a Sanity roll.
temporary_insanity.counterintuitive_note: On this INT roll, success means the investigator fully comprehends the horror and becomes temporarily insane; failure means the mind suppresses or fails to integrate it.

indefinite_insanity.trigger: Lose one-fifth or more of the investigator's starting SAN during one in-game day.
indefinite_insanity.effect: The investigator remains vulnerable to bouts of madness and related effects until recovery under the full rules.
indefinite_insanity.recovery_note: Long-term care and recovery are campaign matters described more fully in the Keeper Rulebook.

sanity_rules.maximum_sanity: Maximum SAN is reduced by Cthulhu Mythos skill: 99 minus Cthulhu Mythos.
table_care: Agree on how loss of control will be narrated.
Do not use the mechanic to mock real diagnoses or players' lived experiences.
The player should remain involved in portraying the investigator whenever practical.
Fade out or revise a result that crosses an agreed boundary.

combat.core_warning: Combat is dangerous. Mythos entities may be stronger than humans, resistant to weapons, or impossible to defeat by ordinary force.

round_structure.initiative: Act from highest DEX to lowest DEX.
round_structure.round_length: Long enough for each participant to take one significant action.
typical_actions: Administer emergency aid when fictionally possible
Take another significant action approved by the Keeper

dodge.tie_rule: A tied level of success favors the defender; the attacker must achieve a better level.

fight_back.tie_rule: A tied level of success favors the initiating attacker; the defender must achieve a better level to counterattack.

close_combat.result: The winner avoids harm; a successful attacker or successful fight-back defender deals damage as appropriate.

firearms.readied_weapon: A readied firearm acts at DEX +50 for turn order.
firearms.multiple_handgun_shots: Firing two or three handgun shots in one round gives one penalty die to each shot.
firearms.point_blank: Within one-fifth of the shooter's DEX in feet, the shooter gains one bonus die.
firearms.defense: A target cannot literally dodge a bullet but may dive for cover. A successful Dodge imposes one penalty die on the attack and costs the target's next attack.

extreme_damage.blunt: Maximum weapon damage plus maximum Damage Bonus, when applicable.
extreme_damage.impaling: Maximum weapon damage plus an additional weapon-damage roll and any applicable Damage Bonus.
extreme_damage.fight_back_limit: A fight-back result normally deals regular damage even if its roll is Extreme.

fighting_maneuvers.purpose: Disarm, knock down, seize, restrain, shove, or achieve another non-damage goal.
procedure: Resolve as a Fighting attack.
The defender may Dodge or fight back.
Compare Build.
The attacker takes one penalty die per point of Build disadvantage, to a maximum of two.
A maneuver is ineffective when the target exceeds the attacker's Build by three or more.

combat.outnumbered: After a character has dodged or fought back once in a round, later melee attacks against that character receive one bonus die. Firearms are excluded.

damage_wounds_and_healing.taking_damage: Subtract damage from current HP; HP does not go below zero.

major_wound.trigger: A single attack deals damage equal to or greater than half maximum HP.
major_wound.immediate_effect: Make a CON roll or fall unconscious.

zero_hit_points.without_major_wound: The investigator is unconscious but is not dying from that injury sequence.
zero_hit_points.with_major_wound: The investigator is dying and must make repeated CON rolls under the full procedure until stabilized or dead.

damage_wounds_and_healing.instant_death: A single attack that deals damage equal to or greater than maximum HP may kill instantly.

first_aid.time_window: Normally within one hour of the injury.
first_aid.effect: Restore 1 HP and potentially rouse an unconscious character.
first_aid.dying_use: Temporarily stabilizes a dying character so Medicine can be attempted.

medicine.time: At least one hour with suitable supplies.
medicine.dying_use: Follows successful First Aid and supports longer-term survival under the full rules.

natural_healing.major_wound: Make a weekly CON healing roll; success restores 1D3 HP and an Extreme success restores 2D3 HP.
natural_healing.major_wound_removed: Removed when an Extreme healing success occurs or current HP reaches at least half maximum HP.

magic_and_mythos_knowledge.tone: Mythos magic is dangerous knowledge that manipulates forces human beings do not safely understand.

magic_points.when_zero: Further magic-point costs are normally taken from HP one-for-one.

first_casting.normal_requirement: A newly learned spell normally requires a Hard POW roll the first time it is cast.
first_casting.pushed_casting: A second attempt may be made by paying the cost again. On a failed pushed casting roll, the spell still operates but dire consequences affect the caster.

magic_and_mythos_knowledge.after_first_success: Later castings of that spell normally do not require the initial casting roll, although the spell's listed costs and procedures still apply.
player_guidance: Do not assume learning a spell is automatically beneficial.
Read, translate, test, and cast Mythos material only after considering time, SAN, magic-point, and narrative costs.
The Keeper Rulebook and scenarios contain the actual spell descriptions.

chases_and_other_advanced_subsystems.status: The complete Keeper Rulebook includes a dedicated chase system and additional optional combat, luck, spending, recovery, finance, magic, and campaign rules.
beginner_method: For a first session, the Keeper may resolve a short pursuit with opposed DEX, Drive Auto, Pilot, Ride, Swim, or another appropriate roll.
Use the full chase subsystem when position, hazards, speed differences, and repeated decisions are important to the scene.
chases_and_other_advanced_subsystems.do_not_mix_rules_casually: Use one declared method for a chase and explain it before the sequence begins.

skill_checks.during_play: When an investigator successfully uses a skill in a meaningful situation, mark its improvement box once.
skill_checks.review: At the Keeper's chosen improvement phase, roll 1D100 for each checked skill.
skill_checks.improvement: If the result is above the current skill value, add 1D10 percentage points.
skill_checks.no_improvement: If the result is equal to or below the current skill, the skill does not increase.
skill_checks.cleanup: Erase the check after resolving the improvement roll.

other_rewards: Sanity rewards defined by the scenario
Cthulhu Mythos knowledge, usually at a serious cost
Changed beliefs, scars, phobias, possessions, or significant relationships
campaign_continuity: Track current and starting SAN for daily loss thresholds.
Track current Luck separately from its starting value.
Update Max SAN when Cthulhu Mythos increases.
Maintain an investigator timeline and case archive.
Prepare a replacement investigator before a long campaign reaches a lethal chapter.

recommended_structure.keeper_goal: Give the investigators a clear reason to act now.
recommended_structure.player_goal: Establish who the investigators are and why they cooperate.

recommended_structure.keeper_goal: Present two or three accessible leads.
Show that the situation is dangerous or unnatural without revealing everything.
Connect earlier clues to a hidden person, location, ritual, object, or event.
recommended_structure.player_goal: Choose which risk is worth taking.

recommended_structure.keeper_goal: Let prior decisions affect the danger and available solutions.
recommended_structure.player_goal: Contain, interrupt, rescue, expose, flee, or confront.

recommended_structure.keeper_goal: Resolve consequences and award improvements or scenario rewards.
recommended_structure.player_goal: Record what changed and decide whether the investigator continues.

keeper_pacing_tips: Start with ordinary reality and introduce the impossible gradually.
Use sensory details beyond sight: sound, smell, texture, temperature, and absence.
Alternate investigation, human interaction, and danger.
Escalate through consequences, not arbitrary punishment.
End scenes once their purpose is complete.
Recap the known facts before the final act.

common_new_player_mistakes.mistake: Treating the game like a tactical monster-fighting campaign.
common_new_player_mistakes.correction: Investigate first. Ordinary weapons may not solve a Mythos threat.
Describe where and how the investigator searches and what they hope to find.

common_new_player_mistakes.mistake: Hiding every clue from the other players.
common_new_player_mistakes.correction: Share case information unless secrecy creates agreed, productive drama.

common_new_player_mistakes.mistake: Assuming a failed roll means nothing happens.
common_new_player_mistakes.correction: Failure often means cost, delay, danger, or incomplete understanding.

common_new_player_mistakes.mistake: Pushing a roll without changing the approach.
common_new_player_mistakes.correction: Explain the new method and accept the announced consequence.

common_new_player_mistakes.mistake: Using Occult and Cthulhu Mythos as synonyms.
common_new_player_mistakes.correction: Occult covers human traditions and esoteric beliefs; Cthulhu Mythos represents dangerous knowledge of inhuman reality.

common_new_player_mistakes.mistake: Building an investigator with no reason to join the case.
common_new_player_mistakes.correction: Create a personal, professional, or relational hook before play.
Escaping with knowledge may be the correct victory.

common_new_keeper_mistakes.mistake: Hiding a vital clue behind one roll.
common_new_keeper_mistakes.correction: Give the core clue when the investigators use a sensible approach; use the roll for speed, detail, danger, or interpretation.

common_new_keeper_mistakes.mistake: Calling for rolls for routine actions.
common_new_keeper_mistakes.correction: Roll only when uncertainty and consequences matter.

common_new_keeper_mistakes.mistake: Requiring the exact solution imagined by the scenario.
common_new_keeper_mistakes.correction: Judge reasonable player plans by their fictional logic.

common_new_keeper_mistakes.mistake: Using Sanity loss as comedy at a player's expense.
common_new_keeper_mistakes.correction: Use the mechanic to support horror and character change within agreed boundaries.

common_new_keeper_mistakes.mistake: Revealing the monster too clearly and too early.
common_new_keeper_mistakes.correction: Let evidence, effects, witnesses, and partial perception build dread.

common_new_keeper_mistakes.mistake: Punishing caution until players rush blindly.
common_new_keeper_mistakes.correction: Allow preparation to matter while maintaining an active threat timeline.

common_new_keeper_mistakes.mistake: Running every NPC as either completely helpful or completely obstructive.
common_new_keeper_mistakes.correction: Give NPCs motives, fears, partial knowledge, and conditions for cooperation.
Advance the scenario timeline when investigators delay, attract attention, or reveal themselves.

ordinary_skill_roll.setup: An investigator with Library Use 55 searches city records for a vanished architect.
ordinary_skill_roll.keeper_ruling: The archive is organized and the investigator has several hours, so a Regular success is enough.
ordinary_skill_roll.result: Regular success. The investigator finds a permit connecting the architect to an abandoned pumping station and checks Library Use for possible improvement.

hard_roll.setup: The same investigator tries to identify a deliberately misfiled deed before the archive closes.
hard_roll.result: Hard success. The investigator notices the false filing and obtains the address before closing time.

pushed_roll.setup: A failed Locksmith roll leaves a cabinet closed.
pushed_roll.new_approach: The investigator removes the hinges with tools, accepting that the noise may alert someone upstairs.
pushed_roll.keeper_stakes: On a failed pushed roll, the cabinet remains closed long enough for the alerted occupant to arrive.
pushed_roll.result_guidance: Roll once more. Apply success or the announced serious consequence.

opposed_roll.setup: An investigator tries to slip past a watchful guard.
opposed_roll.guard_result: Regular success on the relevant opposing ability.
opposed_roll.outcome: The investigator wins because Hard beats Regular.

sanity_roll.setup: A scene lists SAN loss as 1/1D6.
sanity_roll.outcome: The roll fails, so the player rolls 1D6 and subtracts that amount from SAN. If the single loss is 5 or more, the player then makes the temporary-insanity INT roll.

close_combat_dodge_tie.setup: The attacker and dodging defender both achieve Hard success.
close_combat_dodge_tie.outcome: The defender avoids the attack because an attacker must beat, not merely tie, a Dodge result.

close_combat_fight_back_tie.setup: The attacker and fight-back defender both achieve Regular success.
close_combat_fight_back_tie.outcome: The initiating attacker wins because the defender must obtain a better level to fight back successfully.

major_wound.setup: An investigator has 12 maximum HP and takes 6 damage from one attack.
major_wound.outcome: Six is at least half of 12, so the investigator suffers a major wound and makes a CON roll to remain conscious.

quick_reference.roll_under: Roll equal to or below the target.
success_levels: Fumble: 100, or 96–100 when the tested value is below 50
quick_reference.pushing: One justified final attempt with a serious announced consequence; not for combat or Sanity rolls.
quick_reference.bonus_die: Roll an extra tens die and use the lower result.
quick_reference.penalty_die: Roll an extra tens die and use the higher result.
quick_reference.sanity: Roll under current SAN; apply the loss before or after the slash.
quick_reference.temporary_insanity: Single SAN loss of 5+ followed by a successful INT roll.
quick_reference.major_wound: One attack deals at least half maximum HP.
quick_reference.zero_hp: Without a major wound: unconscious. With a major wound: dying.
quick_reference.combat_order: Highest DEX first; readied firearm uses DEX +50.
quick_reference.skill_improvement: For a checked skill, roll above the current value to gain 1D10.

glossary.Call of Cthulhu: Chaosium's roleplaying game of investigation and horror.
glossary.Keeper: The referee and presenter of the scenario.
glossary.NPC: A non-player character portrayed by the Keeper.
glossary.Campaign: Connected scenarios played over multiple sessions.
glossary.Characteristic: A broad innate or developed quality such as STR, INT, or POW.
glossary.Skill: A percentage rating for a learned or practiced capability.
glossary.Regular success: A roll equal to or below the full target value.
glossary.Hard success: A roll equal to or below half the target value.
glossary.Extreme success: A roll equal to or below one-fifth of the target value.
glossary.Fumble: The worst class of result, normally 100 or 96–100 for values below 50.
glossary.Push: A justified second and final attempt after failure, with increased consequences.
glossary.Bonus die: An extra tens die from which the better result is chosen.
glossary.Penalty die: An extra tens die from which the worse result is chosen.
glossary.SAN: Sanity points, a horror-fiction measure of mental resilience.
glossary.Damage Bonus: Extra damage from combined strength and size.
glossary.Build: A relative scale used for physical maneuvers.
glossary.Cthulhu Mythos: Dangerous knowledge of the inhuman Mythos and also the associated skill.
glossary.Bout of madness: A brief acute effect associated with insanity under the game rules.
glossary.Major wound: A serious injury caused by one attack dealing at least half maximum HP.
